newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-PLATINI HOPES FOR SOLUTION ON FENCES FOR WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLATINI HOPES FOR SOLUTION ON FENCES FOR WORLD CUP.

text.p: Michel Platini, joint chief organiser of next year's World Cup in France, said on Friday he was still looking for a solution to meet international calls for the scrapping of perimeter fencing during the tournament.

The world governing body FIFA repeated its viewpoint at a meeting with World Cup organisers that it would rather not have spectators caged in during matches although it realised that security matters were in the hands of the French government.
"It is a matter for the state," Platini said. "But the most important thing is stopping the crowd from getting on the pitch. Maybe we can come up with something."
International officials are worried that fans tend to behave badly when they are "caged in" and want to avoid a repeat of past disasters when spectators have died after being crushed against fences.
The success of last year's largely trouble-free European championship in England, where there were no fences, has also boosted the argument in favour of taking down the cages.
The present view of the French government is that the fences should stay.

But FIFA plans to look closely at an international tournament in France next month when matches will be played in some of the World Cup stadiums and says it is hoping a "flexible solution" may yet be found.
Some French grounds have a moat around the pitch which could be an alternative.

FIFA said it was very impressed with the way the French were preparing for the tournament. The governing body said it was remarkable that the organising committee had already covered 93 percent of its marketing target with sponsorship deals.
Platini said he was expecting all the tickets for the tournament to be sold.
France will provide a precise schedule for matches with kickoff times for the 64 games by September after it has completed a computer survey on climatic conditions at the venues.

"They have to wait to study the exact conditions that they will have in June and July when the finals will take place," a FIFA spokesman said. "There are problems with the position of the sun at the grounds in Bordeaux and Toulouse."
